Shauwn Mkhize Conviction

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
SHAUWN WHO? Glitz and Glamour. Fraud and Tax Evasion. Does fame and fortune get you a clean slate? We investigate the woman behind one of the world’s worst preforming soccer teams.

Summary:
Carte Blanche exposes a questionable government sponsorship only to be dragged to court – accused of getting it wrong.

But did we? We dig even deeper and bring you the facts.

Further information:
CAN THE REAL SHAUWN PLEASE STAND UP?

Flamboyant Businesswoman or Convicted Fraudster?
- Use glam shots, cut to prison bars slaming closed
- But could she be right – did we get it wrong?
- No record of her criminal conviction – But why?
HER TRACK RECORD
- No stranger to insider of a court room… upsound news clips
o We go through the cases…newspaper headlines…. Charges….

She insists that labelling her as a convicted fraudster is false and defamatory.
We search for her criminal record. And came up empty. But this doesn’t add up.
ENTER JJ – she herself admitted to a having a fraud conviction.
But how does that disappear?
ENTER LAYWER
Go for Mkhize Lawyers – dishonest and misleading the court.
LEGAL ELEMENTS TO EXPLORE
1. How did she acquire a police clearance?
2. If her record has been expunged, was she a) legally bound to declare that to the court and b) did she declare that to her attorneys?
3. Her urgent application was withdrawn, but are there any legal implications to her having attempted to mislead the court?
4. Despite her record being expunged, does her conviction not disqualify her from winning government tenders?

INTERVIEWS
 Jonathan Erasmus – journalist. He covered the Mpisanes extensively and had the damning documents where she admits to being convicted of fraud.
 Wesley Rodgers – Criminal Lawyer. He has done hundreds of expungements.

FOOTAGE
- TONNES on social media – photos and videos
- NEWS clips from court appearances filmed by eNCA & the SABC – we could get away with fair use?

TREATMENT
- Glitz and Glam – paparazzi celebrity vibes.
- Behind the scenes filming interview set up – leaning into going behind the façade.

Script:


FINAL SCRIPT – SHAUWN WHO?

VO: Earlier this year - we aired an investigation into the Umsunduzi’s Municipality’s sponsorship of a soccer team, this, despite the town’s apparent dire financial standing.

UPSOUND ROYAL AM STORY:
G VO: A mayor of a provincial capital who seems to be in denial.

G VO: A soccer team owned by a reality TV star, tenderpreneur and convicted fraudster.
ADD IN: MAMMKHIZE - in my case when gods shows up, he shows off.
G VO: And the disturbing question of a 27 million rand sponsorship deal.
MAYOR UPSOUND: Out of sponsoring that team, business thrives in the city.
KANTHA - 10.20 It's quite frustrating ot hear that our monies are being used for a football club.

PAUSE FLASH

VO: It’s a story that landed Carte Blanche in hot water. Shauwn Mkhize is the team’s soccer boss.

GOVAN: You didn't like the story we did about Royal AM and the Umsunduzi municipality.
SHAUWN: Not to say I didn't like it. There were things that I was unhappy about, but I can't decide on your story - it’s your story

VO: The soccer team boss Shauwn Mkhize – now popularly known as celebrity Mamkhize. But formerly known as the infamous Durban businesswoman Shauwn Mpisane. She was not impressed with the investigation, even though she was not actually the focus of the story.

Within days of the broadcast, Carte Blanche was served with an urgent application.

LINK: // And threatened with legal action – the allegation we got it wrong. Shauwn Mkhize says she’s not a convicted fraudster.

VO: The case was set to be heard in the Western Cape High Court within a week. Shauwn Mkhize submitted evidence stating she is not a convicted fraudster, but Carte Blanche has evidence that she is.

To our surprise, MaMkhize’s legal team withdrew the case just two days before the court date.
PAUSE…..
This made us suspicious, and sparked this investigation.

LINK: But this story doesn't start in February this year. To understand it, we need to go back almost two decades. REWIND….

UPSOUND NEWS CLIPS – ENCA & SABC. (10 seconds)

VO: When you Think of MaMkhize and several words come to mind: Glitz and glamour. Fame and Fortune. Fraud and alleged tax evasion.

In the late 2000s, MaMkhize business practices started drawing media attention.

At the time, Investigative Journalist Jonathan Erasmus reported extensively on the Mpisane empire, built on the back of lucrative government tenders.

JJ: They secured almost every single major city housing contract from ethekwini during that time. Some it was it's incredible money. And then they sort of branching out to other parts of the province where they also secured low cost housing projects.

VO: It was their opulent lifestyle that caused SARS to take note, Erasmus believes SARS had a case.

JJ: it was really very standard tax evasion, if you really look at it// at its absolute simplest terms.

VO: He's referring to a much publicised case in 2011. The official charges against MaMkhize and the company, Zikhulise Cleaning, Maintenance and Transport were - tax evasion, fraud, forgery & uttering.

But interestingly, after MaMkhize made submissions the National Prosecuting Authority the case was withdrawn in 2014 - a decision that sparked widespread speculation.

JJ: Shauwn comes from this this political elite that arose out of the in the new democracy who, you know, her mother was Florence Mkhize, a big ANC heavy hitter at the time, // So that just kind of positions her as this daughter coming from this political dynasty if i can use that word

VO: This wasn't MaMkhize's first run-in with the law. She's been charged several times…

PAUSE - CHARGES GRAPHIC

VO: Confusingly, in the summons we received she denied being a convicted fraudster. The documents served on us included this police clearance certificate. We confirmed that some of the cases were withdrawn. But we were baffled, because we knew of one conviction for fraud in 2005.

So convinced of her innocence, Shauwn Mkhize offered a sit-down interview – she wanted to set the record straight.

She brought along an entourage, including her lawyers.

GOVAN: //how would you describe yourself?
SHAUWN: // I don't need to describe myself to anyone. // I will never entertain the noise of the world. // I live in my own world with my own rules..

VO: A phrase that’s become MaMkhize’s motto - ever present on her social media feeds.

JJ: // I think she joins a litany of South Africans that enjoy that kind of right, that rites of passage. I think there's obviously, there's two types of rules in this country. There's the rules for those that are connected and the other rules for those that aren't connected. And she certainly falls into that first category.

VO: Since 2005, it’s estimated that MaMkhize’s enterprise has been awarded over a billion rand in government tenders - from housing projects to public works contracts. But MaMkhize, denies her success is because of her name.

SHAUWN: I never choose to be born in a political environment// Why can't people look at me as a young black woman who has worked very hard, who has pushed boundaries, who has opened doors and break the walls?//
GOVAN: There's this criticism. That you benefited from the stature of, obviously, your mom being an influential person in the liberation movement. And it wouldn't be fair for us to talk about that without asking you. What do you think of of that criticism.
SHAUWN: After you've talked to me today? What's your feeling?
GOVAN: That maybe you're a little irritated by the scrutiny that comes with doing business with the state?
SHAUWN: Do you think I'm a little irritated.
GOVAN: By my questions on that? Yes.
SHAUWN: I'm not irritated. I am I supposed to because now I come from a very strong political background. Family? Am I supposed to shy away from everything because. But if I get it to be because of. Don't you think is a bit unfair?
GOVAN: No, you're not supposed to shy away from it. But I do think that you should expect a level of scrutiny and criticism which will come with it, which is justified because this is is taxpayers money. But I do accept your response to it.

VO: But public scrutiny was amplified when it surfaced in 2011 that MaMkhize and her company were being investigated by SARS.

JJ: It's about trying to pay as little tax as possible and trying to claim tax for things that you're not allowed to claim tax on.

VO: It’s been reported that her run-ins with SARS have also seen her soccer team dragged into the controversy over unpaid taxes in 2023.

GOVAN: // How is it that you live such a lavish life, but you don't pay your taxes?
SHAUWN: Do you really think if you can be audited by SARS today, they will find nothing from you? Do you think you'll be so squeaky clean?
GOVAN: SARS found that you didn't pay a tax. I'm asking you why you didn't pay your tax
SHAUWN: Okay. I think the tax matter is a personal matter. I don't have to divulge here what was my problems between SARS and myself.

VO: We can tell you that MaMkhize tax troubles date back almost two decades.

In court papers filed in 2011 and 2012 - Mamkhize refers to an earlier tax offence from 2005.

JJ: //she in her own words, they said she was convicted // and this is contained in a bail application form

VO: When Mamkhize was arrested for the 2011 case, she applied for bail. This is the bail application. Take note - it’s Mamkhize’s full name. Take note of the charges, and then pay careful attention to the section - Previous Convictions. “One previous conviction in a tax related offence”.

In 2012 - she was arrested for ALLEGEDLY defeating the ends of justice - this is another bail application by MaMkhize. Again, it is stated: “I have one previous conviction for fraud in 2005.”

And that explains our confusion when we were served papers by MaMkhize last month. In the case against us, she produced this police clearance certificate that makes no reference to that conviction, while she persistently states: I am not a convicted fraudster.

To get clarity, we consulted Wesley Rodgers, a criminal defence lawyer.

WES: If you are convicted of a criminal offense and ten years elapses where you haven't been convicted again and convicted of an offense which involves direct imprisonment, or if you are convicted of an offense where you can pay a fine instead of imprisonment up to an amount of 20,000 rand. // you can apply after ten years to have the record expunged.

VO: That means the consequence of the conviction - the criminal record - is scrapped and you no longer have a criminal record.

GOVAN: Does it mean you're no longer a convicted fraudster.
WES: It means you are a convicted fraudster. That's had your record expunged. // the reality is that you were convicted by a court of law.

VO: It appears, this is the most likely reason MaMkhize’s police clearance certificate came up blank.

GOVAN: Did you apply for an expungement of your record?
SHAUWN: I don't know. I don't know. I'm not a lawyer.
GOVAN: Surely you would know if you applied for your record to be expunged.
SHAUWN: That's a big name that you are talking about. And I'm not a lawyer. I don't know what you're talking about.
GOVAN: You don't remember? Or don't want to.
SHAUWN: I don't want to comment about that. All what I can tell you is that my record is clean and all. What I can tell you is that I have never been charged in my personal capacity for fraud.

VO: Rodgers explains in terms of public access - Shauwn Mkhize’s criminal slate is clean. BUT, not all records of the conviction would be wiped.

WES: There will be an internal record of that. The police have got internal records and internal record keeping for their profiling power.

VO: And only the police have access to it. These are printouts from the Crime Administration System on MaMkhize’s ID number - these documents were leaked to Carte Blanche by multiple sources.

This former policeman asked not to be identified, but confirmed the authenticity of these documents.

COP: It's, definitely, drawn from the police system. // she's been charged numerous of times/ There's no two ways about it that whoever this person is with an I.D. number, she's definitely been charged and convicted of fraud on one of the cases

VO: And that’s exactly what MaMkhize said in her personal bail applications.

GOVAN: What did you mean when you said I have one previous conviction for fraud in 2005?
SHAUWN: The company, because that was the company that was charged in 2012.:
GOVAN: Who was convicted of fraud.
SHAUWN: It's the company.
GOVAN: You were the person in the case.
SHAUWN: Was it against me?
GOVAN: It was against you - the conviction was against you?
SHAUWN: Was it against myself?
GOVAN: Yes it was. Okay. It was under your name.
SHAUWN: It did go under my name. Where can you show me?
GOVAN: All right. That's your ID number, isn't it?
That's your I.D. number. What does it say there?
SHAUWN: It says my ID number.
GOVAN: The offense is fraud.
SHAUWN: But what case was this for?
GOVAN: The 2005 case?
SHAUWN: Yeah, but that's was not in my name.
GOVAN: Yes it is.
SHAUWN: No, it was not in my name.
GOVAN: That's your I.D. number? That's your name
SHAUWN: Okay, then what happened to it?
GOVAN: Here it is. The finding at the bottom. So it's fraud and the sentence. Guilty.
SHAUWN: No, but then what happens to it?
GOVAN: This makes you a convicted fraudster.
SHAUWN: No it doesn't.

VO: Yet we have in our possession police records and two VERY DIFFERENT statements made under oath by MaMkhize.

COP: if that was produced to the courts, then she lied under oath, which is perjury

PAUSE

GOVAN: Those are two contradicting statements. Both cannot be true.
SHAUWN: That was for the company, not for my personal. I insist on that. //
GOVAN: But you've been charged with fraud more than once.
SHAUWN: No
GOVAN: 2005, 2012.
SHAUWN: 2012. It was not a fraud. It was tax evasion. 2005 it was because of the income tax number. But I don't even want to dwell on that. And it wasn't me in my personal persona. So that's the business. I have never been charged with fraud in my personal persona. Not once.

VO: The official police records disagree.

COP: She's not telling the truth. //The directors will be implicated.//that's under her personal credentials that she was charged. // She has been convicted, and it's on the system.

GOVAN: //this is not on a company registration number. They're on your I.D. number.
SHAUWN: OK - WHO’S FAULT IS THAT - DO I HAVE TO SUFFER FOR THAT?
GOVAN: You see these pictures here and not of the company logo? They're of yourself. This is from your police profile.
SHAUWN: You are right. When you get charged, you take these photos
GOVAN: So you admit. You know
SHAUWN: I'm saying when you get charged, when you're representing, when there's a case, you get here because you stand in for the company and these are the things that you do.
GOVAN: They took your fingerprints as well when they charged you. Right?
SHAUWN: They always do I think. So I think they do it hink so I think they do.
GOVAN: Ms Mkhize,you're an intelligent woman. I don't believe for a second that you really believe that you were not charged.
SHAUWN: I do. And I categorically believe that it was the company which was charged. And I stand by that, not me. And you'll never make me to change that,//
GOVAN: Well, whether you want to accept it or not, let me say to you that these documents show that you were not only charged with fraud, you were found guilty. Oh, that makes you a convicted fraudster.

VO: As the interview wrapped, MaMkhize got up and left, without even a goodbye. She stuck to her story, despite the facts on the table.

JJ: It's got more to do with her own personality than anything else.
GOVAN: You think Shauwn Mkhize will ever make a clean break from her past?
JJ: //. I think the quickest way to make a clean break is to admit your past and move on. //. // That's essentially that's how we work in this country. You've got to admit fault if it exists.

VO: Weeks after our first story aired, and serving us with court papers, questions remained. But, what we can say with certainty is that Shauwn Mkhize is a convicted fraudster.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): SHAUWN WHO? Glitz and Glamour. Fraud and Tax Evasion. Does fame and fortune get you a clean slate? We investigate the woman behind one of the world’s worst preforming soccer teams.
metadata.Summary: Carte Blanche exposes a questionable government sponsorship only to be dragged to court – accused of getting it wrong. But did we? We dig even deeper and bring you the facts.
metadata.Further information: CAN THE REAL SHAUWN PLEASE STAND UP? Flamboyant Businesswoman or Convicted Fraudster? - Use glam shots, cut to prison bars slaming closed - But could she be right – did we get it wrong? - No record of her criminal conviction – But why? HER TRACK RECORD - No stranger to insider of a court room… upsound news clips o We go through the cases…newspaper headlines…. Charges…. She insists that labelling her as a convicted fraudster is false and defamatory. We search for her criminal record. And came up empty. But this doesn’t add up. ENTER JJ – she herself admitted to a having a fraud conviction. But how does that disappear? ENTER LAYWER Go for Mkhize Lawyers – dishonest and misleading the court. LEGAL ELEMENTS TO EXPLORE 1. How did she acquire a police clearance? 2. If her record has been expunged, was she a) legally bound to declare that to the court and b) did she declare that to her attorneys? 3. Her urgent application was withdrawn, but are there any legal implications to her having attempted to mislead the court? 4. Despite her record being expunged, does her conviction not disqualify her from winning government tenders? INTERVIEWS  Jonathan Erasmus – journalist. He covered the Mpisanes extensively and had the damning documents where she admits to being convicted of fraud.  Wesley Rodgers – Criminal Lawyer. He has done hundreds of expungements. FOOTAGE - TONNES on social media – photos and videos - NEWS clips from court appearances filmed by eNCA & the SABC – we could get away with fair use? TREATMENT - Glitz and Glam – paparazzi celebrity vibes. - Behind the scenes filming interview set up – leaning into going behind the façade.
